name: Baruch
description: Jeremiah's servant living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: Jeremiah calls Baruch the son of Neriah, who writes from Jeremiah's mouth all the words of the Most High upon the roll.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: Baruch does all that the prophet commanded, reading the book of the words of the Most High in the Most High's house.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: Baruch reads the words of Jeremiah in the temple in the chamber of Gemariah, in the ears of all the people.

Michaiah the son of Gemariah, having heard the words, goes down into the king's house to the scribe's chamber where all the princes are sitting, and declares to them all he had heard when Baruch read.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: The princes send Jehudi to bring Baruch with the roll, and they ask him to sit and read it in their ears.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: When they hear all the words they are afraid, both one and another, and say they will surely tell the king; they ask Baruch how he wrote all these words, and he answers that Jeremiah pronounced them with his mouth while Baruch wrote them with ink in the book.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: The princes tell Baruch to go hide himself and Jeremiah, and to let no man know where they are.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: Jeremiah gives a second roll to Baruch, who writes from Jeremiah's mouth all the words of the burned book, and many like words are added besides.

note.label: Jeremiah 36: The Scroll and the Penknife

points: They accused Baruch the son of Neriah of setting Jeremiah against them to deliver them into the hand of the Chaldeans, to be put to death or carried captive to Babylon.

note.label: Jeremiah 43: The Proud Men Reject the Word and Flee to Egypt

points: Johanan and all the captains took the whole remnant of Judah, the men, women, children, and the king's daughters that Nebuzaradan had left with Gedaliah, along with Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch.

note.label: Jeremiah 43: The Proud Men Reject the Word and Flee to Egypt

points: This is the word Jeremiah spoke to Baruch the son of Neriah when he had written these words in a book at the mouth of Jeremiah, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah.
The Most High addresses him directly, "unto thee O Baruch," and the words of the scribe Baruch are preserved in the Apocrypha, so get yourself a 1611 King James Version Bible with the Apocrypha.

cases.name: Baruch the scribe
cases.charge: Writing from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the Lord upon a roll, reading it in the house of the Lord and before the princes, and writing it again after the king burned it
cases.preview: Baruch the son of Neriah wrote in a roll all the words the Lord had spoken to Jeremiah, from Jeremiah’s own mouth, and read them in the Lord’s house on the fasting day while Jeremiah was shut up…
